items.title: 삼성, 미래기술 육성 우수 연구자 10명 선정
items.snippet: 삼성이 14년간 미래기술육성사업으로 지원한 연구자 중 우수 성과를 거둔 연구자를 처음 시상했다.삼성은 5일 서울 강남 웨스틴 서울 파르나스에서 삼성미래기술육성사업 2026 애뉴얼 포럼을 개최했다고 밝혔다.기초과학과 소재, ICT 분야 우수 연구자 10명을 선정했다. 석학으로 구성된 심사위원단이 약 4개월간 평가했다. 644개 연구 과제의 우수성, 확장성, 성장성, 파급력 등을 고려했다.우수 연구자는 삼성의 기술 자문, 기술 교류, 창업, 지식재산권(IP) 멘토링, 후속 연구 지원 등을 받는다.대상자는 오성진 UC버클리대 고등과학원

items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 4일 서울 주택 공급 속도전을 위한 공공재개발 사업 강화를 강조하면서 “조기에 진행될 경우에는 용적률이든 금융 지원이든 각종 인센티브를 강화하면 좋겠다”고 했다. 한국토지주택공사(LH)를 통한 공공재개발의 비중을 높이고 민간 사업의 공공 전환도 쉽게 해 주택 공급에 속도를 내겠다는 것. 이 대통령은 이날도 재차 강남 3구(강남, 서초, 송파구)의 집값이 떨어지고 있다고 강조했다.● “공공재개발 유효성… 인센티브로 사업성 높여야” 이 대통령은 이날 서울 성북구 장위동 일대를 찾아 공공재개발 현장을 시찰하고 정비사업 현장 간담회를 가졌다. 이 대통령은 “확실히 공공재개발 방식이 유효성이 있는 것 같다”며 “공공이 하면 속도도 빨라지고 부정부패 소지도 줄어든다”고 운을 뗐다. 이어 “이 정부에서 각종 인센티브를 제공하기로 했기 때문...

items.title: 李, SNS ‘X’ 이어 유튜브 ‘Y’ 신설… 靑 “소통채널 확대”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 5일 유튜브 프로그램 ‘대통령의 Y’를 시작한다고 청와대가 밝혔다. X(옛 트위터)를 활용한 소셜네트워크서비스(SNS) 소통에 이어 유튜브(Y)로 창구를 확대하겠다는 의도다. 성기홍 대통령홍보소통수석비서관은 4일 청와대에서 브리핑을 갖고 “SNS를 통한 소통 방식에서 더 나아가 유튜브를 통해서 국민의 궁금증에 답하고 정책을 설명하는 프로그램을 만들었다”며 이같이 말했다. 성 수석은 “‘Y’는 이유, 왜를 뜻하는 ‘Why’를 의미하기도 한다”며 “편안한 분위기에서 국민의 언어로 최대한 진솔하게 의견을 피력하고, 국민의 질문에 답변할 예정”이라고 말했다. 청와대는 프랭클린 루스벨트 전 미국 대통령의 노변정담(爐邊情談·따뜻한 난롯가에서 허물없이 나누는 이야기)을 참고한 것으로 알려졌다. 4일 촬영된 첫 방송은 5일 오후 9시에 공개...

items.title: 금융위, 국회 서면답변서 “집값 상승세 당분간 지속”
items.snippet: 금융당국이 국내 주택 가격 상승세가 당분간 계속될 수 있다고 전망한 것으로 4일 파악됐다. 주택담보대출 6억 원 제한 등 대출 규제에 대해선 ‘유지’ 필요성을 강조했다. 국회 정무위원회 소속 국민의힘 신동욱 의원실에 따르면 금융위는 이날 회신한 답변서에서 아파트 가격 전망에 대해 “한국은행 등에 따르면 주택 공급 부진과 그에 따른 주택가격 상승 전망 등을 감안 시 주택가격 상승세는 당분간 지속될 우려가 있다”고 답했다. 금융위는 최근 연간 수도권 아파트 착공 및 입주 물량이 10년 평균치를 밑도는 점, 5∼9월 주택가격전망지수가 ‘1년 내 상승 전망 우세’를 뜻하는 100 이상으로 유지되고 있는 점 등을 가격 상승 전망의 근거로 들었다. 다만 금융위는 “향후 주택 공급 확대, 기준금리 인상 효과 등이 가시화되면 상승세가 점차 둔화될 수 있다는...

items.title: “北해커, 이직 미끼로 바이낸스 엔지니어 낚아… 5개월간 침투 작전”
items.snippet: 북한과 연계된 해커들이 지난달 29일 세계 최대 가상자산 거래소 바이낸스에서 63억4000만 달러(약 8조4454억 원)를 탈취한 해킹을 위해 약 5개월간 치밀한 침투 작전을 벌였다고 바이낸스 측이 3일(현지 시간) 밝혔다. 이들은 가짜 채용 면접과 악성 소프트웨어 유포 등 정교한 공격 수법을 활용해 내부 시스템에 대한 접근 권한을 확보했다. 특히 바이낸스 소속 기술자의 신뢰를 얻어 내부 시스템에 침투한 뒤 가상자산 지갑 관련 핵심 업무를 담당한 다른 직원들의 접근 권한까지 탈취하는 방식으로 공격 범위를 확대했다. 바이낸스는 이날 자체 조사 보고서를 공개하며 이번 해킹을 “정교하게 설계된 다단계 공격”이라고 규정했다. 해커들이 가짜 채용 면접, 악성 소프트웨어 다운로드, 내부 인공지능(AI) 도구 활용 등 다양한 수법을 결합했다고 설명했다.●...

items.title: “공군 1호기 명단 이어 외교부 문서 2건 추가 유출”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령 전용기인 공군 1호기의 탑승자 명단 정보가 유출됐던 악성코드 검사 사이트에 한국 외교부와 관련된 것으로 추정되는 문서 2건이 추가로 유출된 것으로 알려졌다. 1호기 탑승자 명단 파일과 관련해 정부는 이 대통령의 6월 유럽 순방지 소재 해외 공관과 주재국 정부가 교신하는 과정에서 해당 사이트를 이용했을 가능성에 무게를 두고 조사하고 있다. 외교부는 4일 악성코드 검사 사이트인 ‘바이러스토털’에 게재된 외교부 관련 추정 문서 2건의 존재를 확인하고 유출 경로를 조사 중이다. 한 문건은 ‘ROK ICJ_Request for a Bilateral Meeting with the Permanent Representative.pdf’란 이름으로 3월 6일 최초 등록됐다고 한다. 한국(ROK·Republic of Korea)과 네덜란드 헤이그...

items.title: 미래기금 공방, 與 “성장 재원” 野 “총선 사금고”
items.snippet: 국회가 821조 원 규모의 2027년도 정부 예산안 심사에 본격적으로 돌입한 가운데 여야는 162조 원 규모의 미래대응기금을 두고 공방을 벌였다. 정부·여당은 “미래 성장을 위한 재원 비축”이라고 설명했지만 야당은 “초과 세수를 빚 갚는 데 사용하지 않고 ‘총선용 사금고’로 만들었다”고 비판했다. 4일 열린 국회 예산결산특별위원회 첫 종합정책질의에서 더불어민주당 안도걸 의원은 “세수 여력을 일부 미래 대비로 비축한 것은 세수 변동성이란 재정 환경 변화에 대응하기 위한 것”이라며 미래대응기금의 필요성을 강조했다. 같은 당 이건태 의원도 “기술 우위를 유지·확보하지 않으면 후위 그룹이 우리를 추월하고 기회를 상실하게 된다. items.title: [단독]특검 “중앙선관위, 용지부족 투표소 40여곳 투표록 위조 지시”

items.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
items.abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. items.title: Energy Efficient Near-Threshold Voltage Massive MIMO Computing
items.abstract: Near-Threshold Computing (NTC) offers a substan- tial energy savings, i.e., up to 10x, for digital circuits. However, due to Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) variations, low voltage operating digital processors face increased susceptibility to timing errors. This work equips conventional massive MIMO algorithms with computational error detection mechanisms, en- abling reliable operation down to near-threshold voltages. While conventional hardware based Timing Error Detection (TED) systems introduce substantial overhead, this work modifies MIMO algorithms to seamlessly integrate low overhead Algorithm Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT). A co-simulation framework combining transistor level SPICE simulations and workload aware fault injection is developed to investigate reliability, Bit Error Rate (BER), energy savings, and overheads of modified algorithms operating at low voltages. items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. items.abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS$_2$ monolayer and then with a MoS$_2$ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS$_2$, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. items.title: [Dr.이은봉의 의학 연구 다이제스트] 정신질환자, 동조편향 AI 쓰니 망상 더 깊어져
items.snippet: 정신분열증이라고 불린 조현병 환자들은 현실 인식이 떨어져 망상과 환각 증상을 보인다. 망상은 없는 것을 있다고 믿는 것이고, 환각은 없는 것이 보이거나 들리는 현상이다. 최근 대화형 인공지능 챗봇이 확산되면서, 인공지능 사용이 이런 정신병을 일으키거나 정신병을 악화시킨다는 다수의 임상 사례가 보고되고 있다. 이를 인공지능 정신병(AI psychosis)이라고 부르는데, 최근 미국 밴더빌트대 연구팀이 인공지능 정신병 발병 상황을 분석해서 미국의사협회지 정신과 편에 발표했다.

items.title: 가족과 식사하는 남성, 당뇨병 위험 낮아진다

items.title: A Design Rule for Passive Reconfigurable Microwave Devices
items.abstract: Every reconfigurable microwave device places a tuning element - a varactor, a diode, transistor, microelectromechanical or phase-change switch, a ferroelectric or liquid-crystal load - inside a fixed passive network. The network can make a small change of the element produce a large change of the response, and design practice often credits it with the device's tuning capability. This paper shows that a fixed, linear, passive network cannot add to that capability. Each tuning element carries a tuning budget, a dimensionless length computed from its own impedance trajectory, and a fixed passive network can transmit that budget or lose part of it, never enlarge it. items.title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
items.abstract: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number. As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. items.title: NN-Based FeFET Compact Modeling for SPICE Simulation
items.abstract: Prototyping and early-stage circuit evaluation for emerging transistor technologies require fast and accurate compact models for SPICE simulations. Standard physics-based compact models, such as BSIM, offer high fidelity but demand extensive domain expertise and time-consuming equation formulation for every new physical effect, significantly slowing technology development. Neural network (NN)-based models offer a scalable alternative approach, but they rely heavily on smooth numerical solver data with explicit high-order derivative information. However, measurement data suffers from complex noise patterns, making derivative extraction challenging and complicating NN-based transistor modeling. This work presents a derivative-free NN training framework employing spectral normalization to naturally smooth derivative behavior and filter measurement noise. items.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
items.abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_α^{γ+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(ω^r)$ to $L^q(ω^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=α\in(0,1)$, and $ω\in A_{r,q}^+(γ)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_α^{γ+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. items.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
items.abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window...

items.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
items.abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. items.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
items.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. items.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
items.abstract: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

Constructed entirely from publicly available documentation, open source software and measurements on physical hardware, Wolfpine is written in pure Python for readability and ease of modification. items.title: Analytically Calibrated Upper L-Statistics for High-Dimensional Mean Change-Point Testing
items.abstract: This paper develops upper L-statistic methods for testing and localizing a high-dimensional mean change. At each candidate split, the proposed statistics rank the squared studentized CUSUM values across coordinates and aggregate either a fixed number or a fixed proportion of the largest entries. This construction connects max-type and sum-type procedures and provides sensitivity to a wide range of sparsity regimes. We establish asymptotic null distributions under an independent-component representation allowing weak cross-sectional dependence. The limiting laws are Poisson tangent processes for fixed ranks and Gaussian-process or Gumbel laws for proportional ranks. To improve finite-sample performance, we develop analytic calibrations for marginal variance estimation, cross-sectional dependence, extreme clustering, and skewness, and establish their first-order validity. items.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.title: Polariton tweezers
items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. items.title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
items.abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures

The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors...

items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. With our approach, we show that populating quantum dots does not require engineered reservoirs, source/drain bias, ohmic contacts, or in-situ doping. As a result, the num...

items.title: Cryogenic performance of Silicon Photo-Multipliers at LN$_2$ temperature and at 3 K in the RES-NOVA cryostat
items.abstract: Silicon Photo-Multipliers (SiPMs) are semiconductor-based photodetectors that offer performance comparable to that of traditional Photo-Multiplier Tubes (PMTs), while providing several advantages, including low operating voltage, immunity to magnetic fields, compact size, and mechanical robustness. These features have led to their widespread adoption in scintillator-based detectors for both fundamental and applied physics. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in the detection of scintillation light at cryogenic temperatures in low-temperature experiments based on bolometric detectors, such as RES-NOVA and CUPID, as well as in emerging quantum applications. In the RES-NOVA experiment, radiopure PbWO$_4$ crystals are used to detect supernova neutrinos. The scintillation of PbWO$_4$ can only be evaluated at cryogenic temperatures, as the scintillation light yield is negligible...

items.title: Self-driven beta-radiation detection through a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure
items.abstract: Large-volume neutrino observatories, exemplified by IceCube, exploit Cherenkov light generated by neutrino-induced charged particles in Antarctic ice, highlighting the potential of water-based media for high-energy particle detection. In $β$-decay, a neutron converts into a proton via the weak interaction, emitting an electron and an electron antineutrino. The electron constitutes the beta radiation detected in this work, while the accompanying antineutrino motivates future extensions toward neutrino detection. Here we demonstrate a complementary electrical transduction strategy using a graphene/water/silicon heterostructure that generates reversible current transients under beta irradiation at zero applied bias. items.title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. items.title: Cross-Scale Spatial Reasoning: A Learning-Centered Framework for Designing Immersive Learning Environments
items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. items.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In this work, we propose GRAPE (Global Regression with Adaptive Prediction Enhancement), a practical online learning framework for VM in evolving wafer-processing environments. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

items.title: 10 kV $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. The ON/OFF ratio increases with optical power density but exhibits a nonmonotonic bias dependence, reaching approximately 15-...

items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. We interpret these findings with ab initio calculations and an effective spin-circuit model that reproduces the anisotropic magnetotransport. Our results identify the dis...

items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. To address this problem, we propose Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis (UFLD), a novel algorithm that employs reinforcement learning for adaptive measurement acquisition and provides a prediction uncertainty level after each step, stopping the process once sufficient information is obtained. Unlike existing methods that rely on ensemble models or auxiliary confidence estimation deep learning models, UFLD utilizes a more parameter-efficient conformal prediction framework to determi...

items.title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
items.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inel...

items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a...

items.title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
items.abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. We show that we can tailor the spectral absorption of microcrystals samples by controlled...

items.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. SKFitter also identifies missing orbita...

items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. items.title: Growth and morphology of core-shell nanowires incorporating dissimilar hexagonal semiconductors: the case of InAs-ZnTe
items.abstract: Core-shell nanowires incorporating semiconductors from two groups, III-V for the core and II-VI for the shell, have been grown by molecular beam epitaxy in two dedicated chambers connected under ultra-high vacuum, and studied by electron microscopy. During the growth of the shell, the wurtzite structure of the core is replicated in the shell, without any creation of defects. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. items.title: Implementation and Validation of Mismatch-Tolerant High-Gain OTA with a Calibrated Negative Conductance Load
items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. A 6-bit capacitive DAC (CDAC)-based comparator offset calibration scheme enables reliable detection of the sub-millivolt steady state error required for high OTA gain. OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
items.abstract: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. Furthermore, a systematic survey of reported Eu-based Zintl phases uncovers a nearly exponential sc...

items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. Path-integral molecular dynamics shows that the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient at 300 K decreases from 8.14 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2S to 6.72 x 10^-5 and 6.61 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2Se and Bi2O2Te, respectively, despite a 13% larg...

items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. Numerical experiments compare these methods in terms of the admissible time step $Δt$, total simulation time, accuracy against a reference solution and robustness of the schem...

items.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
items.abstract: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surv...

items.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
items.abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: We develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) to evaluate electronic observables without explicitly constructing occupied eigenstates. Nested Fourier probes progressively cancel nearby cross terms, while exponential or algebraic density-matrix decay suppresses distant contributions. Refinement reuses all previous matrix-function responses to evaluate diverse electronic observables. Electron density and nonlocal forces illustrate diagonal extraction and off-diagonal contraction, respectively. A locality-based decay model fitted to changes across completed levels estimates residual errors from the unresolved pairs without additional matrix-function applications. Tests using fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for semiconductors, metals, and thermally perturbed silica cover different decay ranges and periodic cell geometries. About 90% of the assessed density and nonlocal force prediction...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. items.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing
items.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimates guide maintenance in semiconductor manufacturing, where a late intervention can disrupt production but an early one discards usable equipment life. A single prediction does not express the uncertainty needed to choose between these outcomes. We combine Deep Learning (DL) sequence models with Simoultaneous Quantile Regression (SQR) to estimate RUL at selectable quantile levels, and evaluate maintenance decisions using Unexpected Breaks (UB), Unexploited Lifetime (UL), and a cost-weighted objective. On the $F_1$ fault mode of the 2018 PHM Data Challenge (PHM18) ion-milling dataset, we compare recurrent, Transformer, and State Space Models (SSM) architectures. Diagonal State Spaced (S4D) gives the strongest overall RUL accuracy across the evaluated quantiles. Varying the quantile and maintenance window exposes the trade-off between failure risk and earl...

items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. items.title: Fluctuation electrodynamics of quantum capacitance in electron bilayers
items.abstract: Capacitance provides a thermodynamic probe of interacting electrons. It characterizes the energy cost of transferring charge between conductors, which, in low-dimensional systems, is governed by exchange and correlation effects in addition to electrostatic contributions. We develop a theory of the quantum capacitance of electron double layers, semiconductor quantum wells as well as monolayer and bilayer graphene devices, focusing on the contribution generated by interlayer correlations. Within a functional-integral formulation we show that the separation-dependent part of the ground-state energy is, at the level of ring diagrams, exactly the nonretarded Lifshitz expression for the van der Waals energy of two conducting sheets, with reflection amplitudes built from the layer polarizabilities. items.title: Who Needs DRAM? We Have Fiber
items.abstract: The rising pressure on DRAM availability and contract pricing reflects generative AI's massive high-performance memory requirements. This pressure is heavily compounded by hyperscale data center expansion, which now consumes a significant portion of global DRAM output. In this work, we propose a new architecture, Fiber Memory, which reimagines the role of optical fiber in a hyperscale data center, deploying it as an active, recirculating delay-line memory for immutable data, such as large language model weights. We present a hybrid data- and pipeline-parallel optical broadcast delay-line memory architecture that accounts for fiber's physical realities. items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations.
